S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and a disturbance in the way one’s body weight or shape is experienced. Self‑evaluation is often excessively influenced by body shape and weight, and individuals frequently lack recognition of the seriousness of their low body weight. Onset is most common in adolescence and young adulthood but can occur across the lifespan, with a course that may be acute or chronic, often associated with medical complications and high relapse risk. It is distinguished from other eating disorders by the combination of significantly low weight, restrictive intake, and the characteristic body image disturbance rather than recurrent binge eating or purging alone.

patient.personality: Rene is an inquisitive, creative teen who is cooperative yet quietly self‑critical, with a laid‑back attitude toward obligations that contrasts with his intense focus on personal interests like gadgets, gaming, and sketching.
patient.stressor: Rene’s difficulties began in the last two years of high school, when pressure to improve his grades and figure out a concrete post‑graduation plan left him feeling inadequate compared with more high‑achieving classmates and cousins. As he fell behind on assignments despite being bright and capable with hands‑on projects, he started spending long hours online in gaming and sci‑fi forums where discussions around “optimization,” fitness, and self‑discipline framed strict control over food and body as a way to gain mastery and respect. He gradually channeled his anxiety about exams, his uncertain career path, and feeling disorganized into rigid routines around eating and exercising, telling himself that at least he could be “disciplined” in this one area even if school felt chaotic. Over time, family members and a school counselor became alarmed by how thin he had become and how unconcerned he seemed about it, leading his parents to bring him for psychiatric evaluation when he insisted that his weight was fine and that everyone was overreacting.
patient.chief_complaint: “My parents keep saying I’m too thin, but I don’t see what the big deal is.”

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: Most days I just tell my parents I already ate at school, then in reality I’ll pick at a couple of crackers or half an apple in my room and convince myself that’s plenty, because eating a full meal feels like I’m breaking all the ‘discipline’ rules I’ve set for myself from those fitness forums I read.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: Yeah, I know my clothes hang off me and people say I look like I ‘shrunk,’ but when I look in the mirror I just see someone who finally looks kind of lean instead of soft, so it doesn’t feel like a problem.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I even think about having something like pizza or a normal‑sized portion, my brain jumps straight to, ‘You’re going to blow up and lose all the progress you made,’ and I get so anxious I’d rather just drink water and wait it out.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When I step on the scale or see my reflection, that number or how flat my stomach looks basically decides whether I feel like a loser who can’t control anything or at least like I’ve got one part of my life together, even if my grades are trash.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: Everyone keeps warning me about my heart and my energy and whatever, but I still feel like they’re being dramatic, because I can still game for hours, walk to school, and do my little workout routine, so how bad can it really be?
